name: Alex Lindqvist
title: 2nd year B.Sc. in Engineering Physics
summary: Engineering Physics student at Chalmers with a strong background in competitive programming and applied mathematics. Silver medalist in the Swedish Olympiad in Informatics and finalist in the Baltic Olympiad in Informatics, with hands-on experience in C++, Python, and numerical methods. Experienced in developing simulation tools for physics research.

education.narrative: Focus on mathematical modelling, numerical analysis, and programming. Member of the student competitive programming club.
Specialised in mathematics and computer science.
Completed 30 ECTS of university-level mathematics during upper secondary school.

highlights.text: Completed 30 ECTS of university-level mathematics during upper secondary school, including Linear Algebra, Single Variable Calculus, Multivariable Calculus, and Discrete Mathematics. Achieved top grades (A).

experience.title: Laboratory Assistant, Physics Department
experience.narrative: Assisted professors and PhD students with data collection and analysis for condensed matter experiments.

highlights.text: Assisted researchers with data collection and numerical analysis for condensed matter physics experiments.

competitions.name: Silver Medal: Baltic Olympiad in Informatics
competitions.narrative: Top-5 national finish qualified for the Baltic regional olympiad.

highlights.text: Competed against top students from Baltic and Nordic countries, solving advanced algorithmic problems under strict time constraints.

competitions.name: Place 71 / 145: NWERC, ICPC Regional Contest
competitions.narrative: Team of three, five-hour programming contest held in Hamburg.

highlights.text: Participated in a 5-hour team programming contest in Hamburg. As second-year students, ranked 3rd out of 5 Chalmers teams.

competitions.name: Participant: Ericsson AI Hackathon
competitions.narrative: 48-hour industry hackathon focused on applying ML to network optimisation.

highlights.text: Collaborated in a team of five to develop a reinforcement-learning agent for dynamic 5G network resource allocation, reducing simulated drop rates by 18%.
Ranked among the top fifth nationally, demonstrating strong problem-solving, algorithmic reasoning, and independent coding skills.
Maintaining a high competitive programming rating through regular international contests, consistently solving challenging algorithmic problems in C++ and Python.
Organised weekly training sessions and coordinated participation in regional and national contests. Grew club membership from 12 to 35 active members.
